--- title: "[read.read_as_markdown()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Read a document from a path or URL and convert it to Markdown. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/docs-embedding-providers/src/raghilda/read.py#L18-L91){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python read.read_as_markdown( uri, html_extract_selectors=None, html_zap_selectors=None, *args, **kwargs ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is raghilda's entry point for turning a source into a `MarkdownDocument` ready for chunking. It reads the URI (a local file or an HTTP(S) URL) and converts it to Markdown using [MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown), so it handles far more than Markdown files: HTML pages, PDFs, Word (`.docx`) documents, and the other formats MarkItDown supports are all converted to Markdown. For HTML, it keeps the `
` element and removes `
` by default; use the selector arguments to change that. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [uri]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Path or URL of the source to read. Supported forms include: - `path/to/file.md` (or `.html`, `.pdf`, `.docx`, and so on) - `http://example.com/page` - `https://example.com/page` [html_extract_selectors]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : CSS selectors naming the parts of an HTML page to keep. Defaults to `['main']`. [html_zap_selectors]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : CSS selectors naming the parts of an HTML page to remove before conversion. Defaults to `['nav']`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [MarkdownDocument]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The converted content, with `origin` set to `uri` so the source is tracked through chunking and retrieval. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Read a local file or a web page. In both cases you get a `MarkdownDocument` whose `.content` holds the Markdown text: ::: {#3fb288cf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown # Read a local Markdown file doc = read_as_markdown("path/to/file.md") print(doc.content) # Read and convert an HTML page doc = read_as_markdown("https://example.com/page.html") print(doc.content) ``` :::
